issues.t: Cracked dashboard
issues.sym: Cracks open up across the top of the dash and spread until chunks of plastic break loose.
issues.why: The dash plastic on these trucks turns brittle after years of sun and heat cycles.
issues.next: Cosmetic in most cases. A molded dash cap or replacement top panel is the usual repair; remove loose sharp pieces near the airbag area.

issues.t: Intake plenum gasket leak (Magnum V8/V6)
issues.sym: The engine burns oil, puffs blue smoke, pings under load, idles rough or misfires (often on one cylinder) and fouls spark plugs.
issues.why: The intake manifold has a steel bottom plate sealed by a gasket that wears out. Once it leaks, the engine pulls oil and unmetered air into the cylinders.
issues.next: Have the plenum gasket checked and repaired with an updated plate or kit before oily exhaust clogs the catalytic converter or the engine overheats.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing (46RE/47RE)
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, loss of overdrive, a clunk going into gear, or fluid leaks, often after towing.
issues.why: The four-speed automatics in these trucks have weak spots in the torque converter, overdrive and reverse parts, and cooler lines, and they handle heat and heavy loads poorly.
issues.next: Stop towing and have the transmission diagnosed right away. Keep the fluid fresh; a rebuild with upgraded parts is the usual fix once it slips.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure (Magnum)
issues.sym: Hard starting or no-start, stalling while driving, rough idle, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The cam sensor fails or gets fouled, so the computer loses track of engine timing.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A failed cam sensor is a simple part, but stalling in traffic is a hazard, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Ticking from broken exhaust manifold bolts
issues.eng: Magnum engines, 3.7L V6, 4.7L V8, 5.7L Hemi V8
issues.sym: A tapping or ticking noise, loudest on a cold start, that can sound like a lifter. You may also smell exhaust under the hood.
issues.why: Bolts holding the exhaust manifold to the cylinder head snap with repeated heating and cooling, and the joint leaks.
issues.next: Have the broken bolts and gasket replaced before the leak burns the gasket area, upsets oxygen sensor readings or lets fumes reach the cab.

issues.t: Worn front ball joints and tie rods
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering on the highway, uneven front tire wear, or a loose steering feel.
issues.why: The front ball joints and tie rod ends on this generation wear out early, especially on heavier 4x4 trucks.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. A badly worn ball joint can separate, so replace worn parts promptly and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Blend door problems cause weak or one-temperature airflow
issues.sym: Heat or A/C stays stuck at one temperature, comes from the wrong vents, or is weak; you may hear clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: The blend or recirculation doors behind the dash, or the small motors that move them, stop working properly.
issues.next: Have the HVAC doors and actuators checked. It is not a safety issue unless the defroster cannot clear the windshield.

issues.t: Overheating and head gasket failure (4.7L)
issues.sym: Temperature gauge climbing, coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, or milky oil.
issues.why: The 4.7L does not tolerate overheating well; a clogged or cracked radiator or low coolant can lead to blown head gaskets or cracked heads.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if it overheats. Keep the cooling system in good shape and fix leaks right away.

issues.t: Hemi lifter and camshaft wear (Hemi tick)
issues.sym: A ticking noise from the engine that does not go away as it warms, then misfires and a check engine light.
issues.why: Roller lifters can fail and wipe the camshaft lobes, especially on engines that use cylinder deactivation.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed promptly. Driving with a failed lifter spreads metal through the engine and turns a lifter job into a much larger repair.

issues.t: Truck can roll out of Park (recall)
issues.sym: The column shifter can be moved out of Park without pressing the brake, so the truck may roll away.
issues.why: A pin in the brake-shift interlock can stick, defeating the brake-pedal requirement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get it done. Always set the parking brake until it is repaired.

issues.t: Power-locking tailgate can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate opens on its own, sometimes while moving, and cargo can fall out.
issues.why: Parts in the power tailgate lock can crack or bind, letting the latch release.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recalls and have the repair done. Do not carry loose cargo against the tailgate until then.

issues.t: EcoDiesel EGR cooler can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant loss, white smoke, or a sweet smell. In the worst case a fire can start under the hood.
issues.why: The EGR cooler can crack, letting coolant into the hot intake and exhaust gas path.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it completed. Stop driving and have it towed if you see smoke or coolant loss.

issues.t: EcoDiesel high-pressure fuel pump failure (recalls)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving, cranks without starting, or loses power.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can wear internally and stop delivering fuel, which can also scatter metal through the fuel system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall that covers your year and have it done. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not delay.

issues.t: EcoDiesel crankshaft tone wheel can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning and may not restart.
issues.why: The ring the crank sensor reads can separate from the crankshaft, so the computer loses its timing signal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recalls and have the repair done.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The concern shows up only if the curtain airbag deploys.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect can let the curtain airbag inflator break apart when it fires, which can throw metal pieces.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recalls and have the repair done as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Loss of power steering assist (recalls)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a warning light, especially at low speed.
issues.why: A loose ground connection or a short in the electric steering gear can cut power assist.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for both recalls and have them done.

issues.t: Water leak at the third brake light
issues.sym: Water stains on the rear headliner or water at the back of the cab after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Rain gets past the seal of the high-mounted third brake light on the roof.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the bulletin; the fix is a new third brake light assembly. Repair it before water causes mold or electrical faults.

issues.t: Tailgate strikers out of alignment (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate may not latch firmly and can open while driving.
issues.why: The tailgate strikers can be set in the wrong position, so the latches do not grip fully.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the strikers adjusted.

issues.t: Engine stall from computer software (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or at a stop.
issues.why: Engine computer software could command the wrong fuel mixture under some conditions.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall; the fix is a software update at the dealer.

issues.t: Misfires and stalling on the Hurricane HO engine
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire codes on several cylinders, rough running, or stalling.
issues.why: A bulletin found a purge line that can come disconnected, causing misfire codes. Owners have also reported other driveability faults.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the dealer check for the bulletin and stored codes. Get it looked at soon if it stalls.

issues.t: Second row seat belt anchors may not be properly attached
issues.sym: Nothing looks wrong, but the center or left rear belt anchor can pull loose in a crash.
issues.why: The anchor bolts for the second row buckles may not have been installed correctly at the factory.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-495 and have the anchors reattached. Until then avoid seating passengers in those positions.

issues.t: Stability control can switch off from an ABS software fault
issues.sym: The ABS and stability control lights come on and those systems stop helping.
issues.why: Software in the anti-lock brake module can shut electronic stability control down.
issues.next: Have the software updated under recall 24V-653. Normal braking still works, but leave extra room in rain and snow.

issues.t: Turn signal may not cancel on its own
issues.sym: The blinker keeps clicking after you have finished the turn and has to be switched off by hand.
issues.why: The steering column module that cancels the signal can malfunction.
issues.next: Have the module checked under recall 24V-729, and watch your indicator so you are not signaling a turn you are not making.

issues.t: Steering column module weld can stop the driver airbag working
issues.sym: There is no outward sign, though the airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A weld in the steering column module may be faulty, which can break the connection the driver airbag needs to fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-199 and have the module replaced. Do not ignore an airbag light on these trucks.

issues.t: Transmission control unit can leak fluid and cut drive
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive, no response when you select a gear, or the truck will not hold Park.
issues.why: A weld in the transmission control unit can leak fluid and upset the valve body.
issues.next: Have it repaired under recall 24V-413 right away, and always set the parking brake until it is fixed.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go blank from a software fault
issues.sym: The digital cluster goes dark or shows nothing at startup, leaving no speed reading or warning lights.
issues.why: A software error can stop the cluster from displaying.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the software updated under recalls 25V-826 or 26V-225. Driving with no warning lights hides other faults.

issues.t: Damaged wheel hub sensor ring can disable stability control
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights, and the systems stop working.
issues.why: The encoder ring in the front wheel hub can be damaged, so the module gets no usable wheel speed signal.
issues.next: Have the hub assembly replaced under recall 24V-794. Braking still works, but there is no electronic help in a slide.

issues.t: Headlight wiring can make the parking and daytime lights flicker
issues.sym: Parking lights or daytime running lights flicker, dim or go out altogether.
issues.why: Wiring inside the headlight assemblies can lose a solid connection.
issues.next: Have the headlight assemblies replaced under recall 26V-421 so other drivers can see the truck at dusk.

issues.t: Missing clip at the brake master cylinder (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal can suddenly go to the floor with little or no braking.
issues.why: A retaining clip may have been left off the master cylinder push rod, so the pedal can come away from the master cylinder.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Do not drive the truck. Check the VIN for recall 21V-037 and have it towed to a dealer for the free fix.

issues.t: Heated tow mirror glass can come off
issues.sym: The driver side mirror glass loosens, flaps or falls out of the housing.
issues.why: The bond holding the heated glass to the mirror backing can let go.
issues.next: Have the glass replaced under recall 24V-754 and avoid towing or lane changes with a missing mirror.

issues.t: Steering control module fault can affect driver airbag deployment
issues.sym: Usually nothing is noticed, though the airbag light may come on.
issues.why: A fault in the steering control module can keep the driver airbag from deploying the way it should.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-765 and have the module replaced.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensors may miss low pressure
issues.sym: The low tire warning does not come on even when a tire is clearly soft.
issues.why: Faulty pressure sensors may not report or may not trigger the warning light.
issues.next: Have the sensors replaced under recall 26V-623, and check the tires with a gauge every few weeks in the meantime.

issues.t: Power module (TIPM) faults cause no-start and stalling
issues.sym: The truck cranks but will not fire, or the fuel pump keeps buzzing after the key is off, the horn sounds on its own, lights and wipers act up, and some owners have the engine quit while driving.
issues.why: Relays built into the totally integrated power module, the fuse and relay box under the hood, fail inside the sealed unit. The fuel pump relay is the usual one to go.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the module tested instead of replacing one part at a time, and get it done soon. A fuel pump relay that drops out can stall the truck in traffic.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft can break and a wheel can come off (recall 15V-661)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Grinding or clunking from a rear wheel, or a rear wheel that wobbles.
issues.why: Some 2015–2016 Ram 1500 trucks built from June 17 to September 28, 2015 got rear axle shafts that were not heat-treated properly. A shaft can break and the wheel can separate from the truck (recall 15V-661).
issues.next: If you hear grinding or clunking from a rear wheel or the truck feels unsteady, slow down and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 15V-661.

issues.t: Front half-shaft can break (recall 16V-301)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front, then grinding or vibration.
issues.why: Some 2016 Ram 1500 trucks built from February 19 to March 3, 2016 got front half-shafts that were made wrong. One can break without warning and throw parts onto the road (recall 16V-301).
issues.next: If you hear a bang from the front followed by grinding or vibration, slow down, pull over where it's safe and have it towed. Check your VIN for recall 16V-301.

issues.t: Electric power steering assist can cut out (recall 16V-167)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly turns heavy, especially at low speed, and a warning light may come on.
issues.why: On some 2015–2016 Ram 1500 trucks built from January 22 to September 13, 2015, contamination on the power steering circuit board can short it out and cut power steering assist (recall 16V-167).
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for recall 16V-167.
